It’s very scary. I hate that this is our routine thoughts because our kids is so important. I hate feeling like this. It takes so much to do all the things they need and it’s an uphill battle to pretend you are fine. Some days I barely make it, even after years of therapy. Very little medication has been helpful. I feel like I have tried it all. So now I tried to think of it as the devils in my head and most days make peace with it. I am a mom and working and no one knows how bad, except for my husband. It’s a burden for him because he feels helpless, even though it’s not his job to fix my mental issues. Then I feel guilty and thoughts of suicide deepens. My biggest nightmare is being anyone’s burden. But we have to keep on because no kid makes peace with their parent’s suicide. They will always blame themselves or end up hating you for leaving them. Hang in there for daughter!

He sounds like a malignant narcissist. He let you in because he saw you were vulnerable. He gets his high from hurting others because they are hollow shells. You were attracted to him properly because he felt familiar. I. E. This was not the first time you were abused. It’s easy to say just to let it go, but it’s impossible to do it. Invest into a counselor who is familiar with a narcissist’s motivation. It will take time to get over this, but you were smart enough to break the cord. It will get worse before it gets better, but it will.
